lines: CoinGecko full history failed for 14 coins (full history refused by the plan; last year only); the key in this run: basic.

21 listed coins (AI, TROLL, CARDS, BUTTCOIN, USELESS, TTT, WIF, POPCAT, AI16Z, BONK, FARTCOIN, PNUT, GOAT, MOODENG, HAWK, LIBRA, MELANIA, PONKE, PEPE, TRUMP, SPX) left out: older than the free candle feed reaches (about six months), so the launch is not in the data. Pools picked by symbol search (check these are the real coins): CASHCAT = Cash Cat, AI = Artificial Inu, PONS = Pons, TTT = TokenTime Two, LIBRA = LIBRA.
5 giants studied. The typical one took 54 days from launch to its top, went 51.02x from the day-1 close, and on the WAY there fell 30%+ 9 times and 50%+ 6 times (worst dip before the top: 95%).

So a rule that sells everything on a 50% giveback is out of the typical giant before the top: the clips must fund the ride, and the moonbag must trail wider than a giant's dips (95%+), or it never sees the top.

From a $500 entry on the day-1 close, summed over all 5: hold $97,688, trail35 $5,898, giveback $5,486, clipsTrail35 $4,980, clipsTrail50 $4,968, clipsTrail65 $4,839, trail50 $4,613, trail65 $3,229 (the exact top would have been $294,851). Best rule: hold: never sold (rode it to wherever it is now).

Entry day against the multiple to the top (median): day 0 84.63x, day 1 51.02x, day 2 43.75x, day 3 60.63x, day 5 37.76x, day 7 38.26x, day 14 13.01x; the first 30% pullback after a 2x: 51.02x (5 of 5 gave one).
After the top: 1 of 5 are now 80%+ under it (median 20 days to lose half from the top). Riding it back is the default outcome; the rules above are what stand between a $500k position and zero.

Day-3 fingerprint, giants against 4 duds (coins that pumped and died): on day 3 the giants stood at 0.93x their day-1 close with 0.85x day-1's volume and 40% were still above the day-1 close; the duds at 1.02x, 0.28x the volume, 50% above. Not a clean separation yet: add more duds and giants to src/giants.json.
